3. Data Sources

Observed Data

Observations come from two main types of sources:

  • Antarctic ice cores. Measurements of gases trapped in layers of ice are available here through 2001 for carbon dioxide, 1980 for methane, and 1976 for nitrous oxide.
  • Atmospheric monitoring stations. Data come from monitoring stations in Hawaii, Alaska, American Samoa, Australia, Scotland, Italy, and the South Pole. The earliest series is carbon dioxide at Mauna Loa, Hawaii, starting in 1959; other sites started subsequently, and some continue to operate.

The technical documentation for the Atmospheric Concentrations of Greenhouse Gases indicator provides publications, links, and other details for each source data set.

Model Outputs

This pairing presents the official greenhouse gas concentration projections from the Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSP) Database, Version 2.0. These concentrations have been used as inputs to the global climate models (GCMs) within the World Climate Research Programme (WCRP) Coupled Model Intercomparison Project Phase 6 (CMIP6) suite.

4. Data Availability

Observed Data

The observed data used to develop this pairing are publicly available and can be accessed from the references listed in the technical documentation for EPA’s Atmospheric Concentrations of Greenhouse Gases indicator.

Model Outputs

Projections were downloaded from the SSP Database. The team specifically used Version 2.0, released December 2018. These outputs are publicly available to any user who creates a free guest login.
